problem: The temperature, in degrees Fahrenheit, of a rapidly cooling substance after $t$ minutes can be modeled by the function $F(t)=250-{t}^{3}.$ Find the instantaneous rate at which the temperature of the substance is changing with respect to time at the moment when the temperature of the substance is equal to $34$ degrees Fahrenheit.

examples.knowledge_point: Determining a Rate of Change for a Given Function at a Point
examples.problem: Lizzie buys $b$ pounds of bananas at a price $p,$ in dollars, that can be modeled by the function $p(b)=5e^{-0.2b}.$ What is the instantaneous rate of change of the price when $b=5$ pounds?
examples.worked_solution:
The instantaneous rate of change of the price when $b=5$ pounds is equal to $p'(5).$

First, we take the derivative and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{p}^{′}(b) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}b}(5{e}^{-0.2b}) \\  & =5{e}^{-0.2b}\cdot (-0.2) \\  & =-{e}^{-0.2b}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $b=5,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{p}^{′}(5) & =-{e}^{-0.2(5)} \\  & =-{e}^{-1} \\  & =-\frac{1}{e}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate change of the price when $b=5$ pounds is $-\dfrac{1}{e}$ dollars per pound.

feedback.problem: The function $P(t)=710\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+{e}^{t})$ represents the volume of milk, in liters, produced on a farm $t$ days after the owner bought new cows. What is the instantaneous rate of change of the volume of produced milk as a function of $t?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The instantaneous rate of change of the volume of produced milk with respect to time is ${P}^{′}(t).$

Now, the rate of change of $P(t)$ with respect to $t$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(710\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+{e}^{t})) \\  & =710\,\frac{{e}^{t}}{1+{e}^{t}} \\  & =\frac{710}{1+{e}^{-t}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate of change of the volume of produced milk is  $\frac{710}{1+{e}^{-t}}$ liters per day.
